situation: On a windy day in Garoua, Moussa stands by the Benue. The wind blows on the water and makes small waves that move towards the bank.
His cousin in Kribi says that on the Atlantic Ocean, the waves are very big and powerful. Moussa wonders what a wave is, and why some waves are small and others very strong.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Moussa does not know what a wave is and why waves have different strengths.
What makes the waves on the Benue?
The wind blowing on the water makes the waves.

qa.a: A wave is a movement of energy through the water of the sea, which makes the surface rise and fall. The water moves in circles; the energy moves forward.
Most waves are caused by the wind blowing over the surface of the sea.

qa.q: On what does the size of a wave depend?
qa.a: It depends on the strength of the wind, how long it blows, and the fetch: the distance of open water over which the wind blows.

qa.q: What are the swash and the backwash?
qa.a: The swash is the water that rushes up the beach when a wave breaks. The backwash is the water that flows back down the beach.

sum.title: I. Meaning of Waves
defs: A wave is a movement of energy through the water, which makes the surface of the sea rise and fall. Most waves are caused by the wind.
items: – The fetch: the distance of open water over which the wind blows.
– Swash: water that rushes up the beach after a wave breaks.
– Backwash: water that flows back down the beach to the sea.

qa.q: What are constructive waves? What do they do?
qa.a: They are low, long waves (about 6–8 per minute) with a strong swash and a weak backwash. They bring sand and build the beach.

qa.q: What are destructive waves? What do they do?
qa.a: They are high, steep waves (about 11–15 per minute) with a weak swash and a strong backwash. They remove sand and erode the coast.

sum.title: II. Types of Waves
sum.intro: There are two types of waves:
items: Low, long waves, about 6–8 per minute. The swash is stronger than the backwash, so they bring sand and build wide, gentle beaches. They come in calm weather.
High, steep waves, about 11–15 per minute. The backwash is stronger than the swash, so they take sand away and erode the coast. They come with storms.

evaluation: The wind blowing over the sea.
The fetch is the distance of open water over which the wind blows.
What is the difference between constructive and destructive waves?
Constructive waves have a strong swash and build beaches; destructive waves have a strong backwash and erode the coast.
remediation: Most waves are caused by the ______.
The distance of open water over which the wind blows is the ______.
Water rushing up the beach is the ______.
Water flowing back to the sea is the ______.
Waves that build beaches are ______ waves.
Waves that erode the coast are ______ waves.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. wind 2. fetch 3. swash 4. backwash 5. constructive 6. destructive
